title: Autoscorer blueprint for customer network preflight with risk explainability
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Customers requesting private/VPC/on-prem deployments frequently submit environment details that are inconsistent or incomplete, causing long manual triage cycles and surprising upgrade downtime. We need an automated, explainable preflight autoscorer that assigns a reproducible risk score to an incoming request and highlights the top contributing signals so PMs/SEs can prioritize, communicate, and remediate faster.

Goals:
- Reduce manual triage time for new private/VPC/on-prem intake by 40% for medium/high risk requests.
- Surface a deterministic numeric risk score (0-100) plus top 3 contributing signals and a suggested remediation path.
- Be safe for air-gapped customers (no outbound probes without consent) and respect PII/network secrecy constraints.
- Integrate score and explanation into intake UI and handoff workflows for Solutions Engineering and Eng on-call.
acceptance_criteria: Autoscorer returns a numeric score between 0 and 100 for every new intake request within 5 seconds of submission.
Response includes top 3 contributing signals (e.g., asymmetric firewall rules, unsupported outbound ports, L3 NAT overlap) with a short natural-language explanation for each.
Intake UI shows score badge + one-click 'request probe' or 'send guidance' actions depending on customer consent and deployment isolation level.
Telemetry logged to onboarding dashboard: score distribution, remediation acceptance rate, time-to-resolution; accessible to PM/SE/Eng with RBAC.
Security review signed off on probe behaviour and no customer secrets are exfiltrated; automated probes default to dry-run mode for air-gapped profiles.
Manual override path exists: Solutions Engineer can bump/reduce score and add a rationale; changes are auditable in the ticket history.
Integration tests cover 6 canonical failure modes (DNS blocked, blocked outbound 443/80, corporate proxy rewrite, overlapping CIDRs, MTU limitations, blocked NTP) with expected score bands.
plan: Week 1: Finalize scoring rubric and signal taxonomy (owner: PM Asha). Deliver canonical signal list + weightings.
Week 2: Prototype server-side scoring API (owner: ENG - L3 infra) + basic UI slot in intake flow (owner: UX - Maya Chen).
Week 3: Implement optional in-customer probes (consent-first) and dry-run probe mode for air-gapped cases (owner: ENG - Platform).
Week 4: Integrate explanation generator (short templates) and telemetry events (owner: Observability team).
Week 5: Security review & privacy checklist, sign-off (owner: Security).
Week 6: Pilot with 3 enterprise customers in staggered rollout, collect feedback, tune weights, and update runbook.
notes: Signal taxonomy should avoid any direct packet capture or payload inspection; only metadata and connectivity fingerprints are permitted without explicit customer approval.
Tradeoff: aggressive scoring reduces risk but increases false positives and engineering handoffs; aim for high recall on critical failure classes and offer clear remediation templates.
Probe patterns: prefer passive checks (port reachability, DNS resolution) and a single optional active probe that can be run by customer's SE in their environment via a signed bundle.
Explainability: deliver both 'why' (top signals) and 'what to do' (priority remediations + estimated effort in hours).
Data retention: scoring inputs stored for 90 days by default, with a customer toggle per contract for extended retention.

security_considerations: All probe binaries must be signed and reviewed; default is no outbound probes for air-gapped customers.
Scoring inputs that could contain network identifiers are treated as sensitive PII-equivalent and masked in analytics exports.
Consent audit trail must persist and be surfaced on the ticket before any active checks are executed.
